# Chronological pitcher backtest (amendment 11; generated by `python -m src.backtest_chrono`)

Every predictor of a pitcher arriving in season Y uses only data from before his first CPBL game: AAA Y-1 (for 2024-25 arrivals the 365-day window before that game, which for three 2025 arrivals includes 471-748 AAA pitches thrown early in 2025), CPBL REBAS seasons before Y, and earlier arrivals' outcomes. 2024 arrivals have no chronological Fit (no REBAS season before 2024). This is a retrospective evaluation with chronological inputs, not a replay of model development: the baseline weights were chosen from 2025-26 AAA diagnostics, and the cohort and its outcomes were already known (amendments 2 and 7), so it is not a fresh confirmation. 2024-25 outcomes: 資料來源：野球革命 Rebas Open Data; 2026: stats.cpbl.com.tw (limitations L10).

Cohort n = 17 (by arrival season {'2024': 8, '2025': 7, '2026': 2}).

Reference pools: 2024: AAA 2023, baseline pool 658, no Fit; 2025: AAA 2024, baseline pool 624, Fit env REBAS [2024], reference pool 611; 2026: AAA 2025, baseline pool 634, Fit env REBAS [2024, 2025], reference pool 611

Limits: the cohort is selected on CPBL survival (>= 60 BF) and on prior AAA tracking; only 7 (2025) + 2 (2026) pitchers have a chronological Fit; nothing here measures recruitment success or validates the candidate pipeline; intervals are pointwise (eight tests, no multiplicity correction) and condition on the estimated scores and environments; 2026 outcomes are centred on the mean of the six club rows and screened on approximate BF (limitations L7). The reference pool counts tracked pitches as the ranking does (pitches Fit can use); counting every tracked pitch gives pools of 612 / 614 and leaves C1 at 0.73.
